title.narrative: Response to Urgent and Critical Needs for the Education Sector

description.narrative: ltpgtltspangtDespite severe constraints, UNICEF continues to support access to learning at scale in the Gaza Strip. As of April 2026, UNICEF is supporting 226,777 students (107,149 girls) through 153 UNICEF-supported learning centres (LCs). UNICEF as a Cluster Lead Agency is a pipeline partner for the procurement and delivery of key education supplies in the Gaza Strip. The Education Cluster consolidates pipeline supplies based on need and facilitates distribution to Cluster partners. UNICEF has fundraised through multiple donors to fulfill its pipeline commitment and plans to reach 1,020,000 children (more than the total children in need for one school year) with essential supplies through funding from other donors. The project is intended to finance the remaining gaps under common pipeline (high-performance tents and tarpaulins) as this is an area which UNICEF has demonstrable success in receiving across the border and tents remain a key priority for the Education Cluster for distribution to partners as part of the larger education response.lt/spangtlt/pgtltpgtIn addition to acting as a pipeline parter, UNICEF has also been recommended because of its multi-sectoral, sustainable approach to implementing quality learning centres that are co-managed with the MoEHE across all areas of the Gaza Strip. NGO partners often establish temporary learning spaces but are unable to support the recurring costs of running the TLS. The MoEHE therefore contacts UNICEF to provide ongoing support based on the UNICEF-MoEHE standard model. UNICEF’s strategy aims to expand access through both Cluster partner-identified and UNICEF-identified sites to reach at least half of the total children in need across the Gaza Strip, while providing key supplies for other partners consolidated by the Education Cluster—complemented through multiple sources of funding for the common pipeline.ltbrgtThe project contributes to the Education Cluster Flash Appeal outcomes by restoring safe, inclusive learning opportunities for crisis-affected children through provision of essential supplies to rapidly identify learning spaces and rehabilitation and expansion support to fully operate 8 LCs. This will benefit a total of 51,300 learners: 42,800 learners through the provision of high-performance tents to Education Cluster partners and 8,500 learners through sustained support for learning in 8 LCs. The project will work closely with the Education Cluster to identify needs for high-performance tents and to support delivery to partners. Partners will then utilize the tents to establish learning spaces in coordination with UNICEF and the MoEHE. As part of the scale-up of UNICEF-MoEHE learning centres in line with the Flash Appeal objective, some LCs identified by Cluster partners will be referred to UNICEF. The target is to increase 8 LCs’ capacity to absorb children through light rehabilitation, and by furnishing and equipping classrooms, including with student and teacher supplies. Education personnel will receive targeted capacity building according to their role, including accelerated learning, social and emotional learning, child protection referral pathways, safeguarding/prevention of sexual exploitation and abuse, and disaster risk reduction. The 8,500 children will be screened for disabilities (vision, hearing and speech) to identify barriers to participation and improve inclusion, including informing individual learning plans, classroom adaptations, and referrals.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtUNICEF works through multiple modalities depending on the availability of safe education infrastructure. Across the Gaza Strip, Learning Centres are identified (a) in existing school buildings which can be rehabilitated to accommodate education services, (b) existing community initiatives or NGO-initiated sites (where funding was not available to continue or has run out) which are handed over to UNICEF and the MoEHE to operate, and (c) vacant spaces that can be cleared for children to attend school safely.ltbrgtlt/pgt
